text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — high GPU queue growth in region us-east1 (spot-pool). auto-scaler reported consecutive failures to provision additional GPU nodes for the last 3 minutes. Severity: P1 :rotating_light:

sam (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Paging lee for handoff if this goes long.

anya (eng-runtime): Looking at the serving queues — > 2k pending requests across shard-a. Token-throughput SLO violated for multiple customers.

mike (infra): autoscaler logs show API errors from cloud: 
```
Error: QuotaExceeded: Requested GPUs exceed quota for project
attempt to create 8 x nvidia-a100 failed
```

sam (oncall): That matches the cloud console. Quota shows available GPUs = 0. But spot capacity also had multiple preemptions in the last hour. Any fallback pools?

anya (eng-runtime): We have reserved pool d-spot-reserve but it's sized to 10 gpus and it's already pinned to other tenants. Fallback routing to cpu fallback exists but returns degraded outputs and isn't enabled by default.

beth (support): We're already getting CS pings — customers A and C report timeouts and 429-like throttles surfaced as "service overloaded" in logs. 

jordan-sre: Adding context: autoscaler attempted to scale from 40 -> 64 GPUs but API didn't create nodes. Our internal circuit breaker flipped after 4 failed create attempts and stopped further attempts. I see the breaker message: `scale_attempts_suspended=true`

sam (oncall): Quick mitigation plan: 1) Pause non-critical background jobs to free queue, 2) Enable limited cpu-only fallback routing for low-priority requests, 3) Request emergency quota bump with cloud support, 4) If quota not available, spin up smaller GPU instances in a different region and route traffic. I'll start 1 & 2 now.

anya (eng-runtime): I can flip the routing flag. Will do a conservative CPU-fallback that routes model-light requests to a CPU pool and returns explicit note for customers. Code to toggle (internal feature flag):
```
POST /flags/enable
{ "flag": "cpu_fallback_limit", "value": "true", "limit": 200 }
```

sam (oncall): Do it, but set limit=100 to be safe. Annotate with incident id INC-2026-1826504321.
\
anya (eng-runtime): Done. `cpu_fallback_limit=100` enabled. Now watching queue.

deploy-bot: deploy 1826504321-cpu-fallback rolled out to edge-routing (3/3 pods ready) :white_check_mark:

mike (infra): Opening support case with cloud now. Case 0267 opened — asked for emergency GPU quota for 50 units. ETA from cloud support ~ 45-90m.

sam (oncall): We still need immediate relief. Can we throttle incoming traffic to hosted API keys with highest request rates? Beth, can support identify top affected tenants?

beth (support): Yes — customer-A, customer-B, customer-C are top noisy tenants. I'll prepare a message and coordinate rate-limit application with you.

anya (eng-runtime): Suggest route-level throttles: reduce max_concurrency for chat endpoints from 8 -> 2 for non-enterprise plans. That'll shed load quickly. Patch snippet: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: chat.gen
    max_concurrency: 2
```

sam (oncall): Apply the route change as a short-term throttle. @mike can you approve a config patch?

mike (infra): Approved. Pushing config now.

deploy-bot: config-update 1826504321-route-throttle applied to hosted-api (success) :rocket:

sam (oncall): Monitoring effect... queue length dropping from 2100 -> 1400 over last 2 min. CPU fallback handling ~60 requests. Still see ~10% of requests failing with 503 from kv-cache misses.

jordan-sre: Noted that preemption rate spiked 12% 10m ago. Cloud spot advisory shows regional capacity pressure in us-east1. If quota bump blocked, cross-region shift is next but will add latency and require model fallback adjustments.

beth (support): Draft message for customers: "We're experiencing degraded performance in US-East due to spot GPU interruptions and autoscaler failures. We're throttling non-enterprise traffic while we remediate. ETA initial mitigation: 30-60 minutes." Shall I send?

sam (oncall): Hold until we confirm stable under throttles. If queue keeps dropping and key customers are within SLOs (best-effort), send at T+20.

anya (eng-runtime): Additional telemetry: redis queue backlog shows head latency spikes originating from shard-a-03 where node churn > 3 in last 30m. Suggest pinning shards away from that node group temporarily. I can patch scheduling affinity: 
```
kubectl patch statefulset shard-a -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"scheduling":"avoid-group-a"}}}}}'
```

sam (oncall): Do it. Try to avoid more preempt-prone pools.
\
anya (eng-runtime): Patch applied. Observed initial pod reschedules. New pods pending due to GPU quota — we won't get new GPU pods until quota resolved but at least we stop rescheduling on volatile hosts.

mike (infra): Cloud responded — they can add ephemeral quota on approval but need validation of business impact. I sent usage metrics and CS tickets. ETA now 40m.

sam (oncall): Okay. Current state: throttles + cpu fallback + shard affinity patch in place. Queue ~900 and trending down. Customer impact reduced but degraded for some heavy customers. I'm going to escalate to engineering manager and hand off to lee (oncall-next) for ongoing until quota resolved. Leave detailed notes.

sam (oncall): Handoff -> @lee: Current mitigations in place: route throttles, cpu_fallback_limit=100, shard affinity patched, cloud case 0267 open. Next steps for you: 1) keep monitoring queue + 95/99 latency, 2) if cloud quota denied, execute cross-region routing plan (runbook link below), 3) coordinate with support on customer comms. Incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-1826504321/runbook

lee (oncall-next): Acked. I'll take over monitoring. If queue stops dropping in 15m, will trigger cross-region plan. Also will prepare selective emergency releases to reduce model sizes for heavy customers.

beth (support): I'll queue the customer message for send at T+20 unless you ask me to send earlier.

sam (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving status: Mitigated (partial), P1 open, oncall handoff complete.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: ONCALL_HANDOFF -> MONITORING. Incident assigned to lee (oncall-next).
